uslaw-usc-t1-s1:
Section 1 of Title 1 of the United States Code sets rules for how words in acts of Congress are to be read. It sits in Chapter 1 of that title, on rules of construction. Unless the context shows a different sense, set rules hold. Words in the singular cover several persons, parties, or things as well. Words in the plural cover the singular in turn.

Words of the masculine gender cover the feminine as well. Words used in the present tense cover the future as well as the present. The terms insane and insane person are stated to cover each idiot and insane person, as the list goes on. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1:
Section 1 of Title 2 of the United States Code sets the time for electing United States Senators. Title 2 governs Congress itself, and its first chapter covers the election of Senators and Representatives. The rule ties a Senate election to the regular election calendar of each state.

A Senator is to be chosen at the regular election held just before his term runs out. That election must be one at which a Representative to Congress is regularly chosen by law. The people of the state do the electing under this section. The winner's term then begins on the third day of January that follows. The text is short, but it fixes the rhythm by which Senate seats change hands.
